# SquadAir

> SquadAir (`https://squadair.app/`) is a free, open-source (GNU AGPLv3) pure-Rust peer-to-peer voice chat and 1080p60 screen sharing desktop client for Windows, macOS (Apple Silicon), and Linux. Built for competitive shooters with zero accounts, zero subscription tiers, and zero central media servers.

## Key Benchmarks & Architecture

- **Memory & CPU Footprint:** `~48 MB` RAM and `< 1.5%` CPU during an active voice call with `1080p 60fps` screen sharing (`~36–46 MB` voice-only), dropping to `~3.5–6 MB` working set (`< 0.2%` CPU) when minimized to the Windows system tray via `SetProcessWorkingSetSize`.
- **Native Binary & Installer Sizes:** Pure Rust `iced` 0.13 desktop client (`~21 MB` typical footprint; `11.6 MB` macOS ARM64 `.pkg`, `34.7 MB` Windows `x86_64` `.exe` installer, `11.7–15.3 MB` Linux `.deb` / `.rpm` / Arch / `.tar.gz` packages); self-hostable `squad-rendezvous` coordinator binary is `1.7 MB` (`2,768 KB` live RSS).
- **Real-Time Audio DSP (`squad-dsp`):** Lock-free `cpal` + `ringbuf` SPSC audio engine, `rubato` resampling, `10 ms` Opus frames (`24 / 40 / 64 / 96 kbps`), WebRTC `AEC3` acoustic echo cancellation, `RNNoise` and optional `DeepFilterNet3` noise suppression, and adaptive jitter buffer profiles.
- **Free 1080p60 Screen Sharing (`squad-video`):** `720p / 1080p / Native` at `30 / 60 FPS` with zero subscription tiers — DXGI Desktop Duplication on Windows and CoreGraphics on macOS, hardware H.264/H.265 encoder detection (`VideoToolbox`, `NVENC`, `AMD AMF`, `Intel QSV`), 4-lane parallel stripe codec (`IDR_MODE_JPEG_STRIPED`), atomic `64x64` tiles, interleaved `XOR-FEC`, direct `wgpu::Texture` shader playback, and `0%` capture/encode load when unwatched.
- **Zero-Knowledge Cryptography (`squad-proto`):** End-to-end `ChaCha20-Poly1305` AEAD sealing every voice frame, video fragment, chat message, inline clipboard screenshot (`Ctrl/Cmd+V`), and `1024 B` P2P swarm file chunk; room keys derived client-side via `BLAKE3` from a 256-bit secret; 128/2048-packet replay windows; `X25519` dual-DH `sqf_` friend invites; `SPAKE2` (`Ed25519Group`) for 6-digit voice codes (`482-910`) and password-locked LAN rooms.
- **3-Tier UDP Mesh & Stateless Coordinator (`squad-rendezvous`):** Tier 1 direct P2P or zero-config LAN UDP mesh (`< 1 ms` LAN with automatic host failover); Tier 2 automatic 1-hop peer-mesh relay for asymmetric NATs (voice, chat, and video); Tier 3 opt-in stateless voice and chat relay on `rv.squadair.app:3478` (`<= 320 B`, `150 pps` per peer, heavy video opcodes blocked, unauthenticated sources dropped silently). Supports up to 10 peers per room over a single UDP port (`3478`) with Docker `read_only` support.
- **Desktop Workspace & Overlay (`squad-client`):** Native GPU-accelerated UI with click-through left-center in-game HUD overlay (Win32 `WS_EX_TRANSPARENT` / macOS AppKit `ignoresMouseEvents`), `5x5` BLAKE3 deterministic identicons, and zero email, phone number, or account requirements.
- **Open-Source License:** Released under **GNU AGPLv3** (`AGPL-3.0-only`).

- [Privacy Policy & Zero-Knowledge Disclosure](https://squadair.app/privacy.html): Technical disclosure of ephemeral coordinator RAM state and local-only client configuration.

- [Security Contact (RFC 9116)](https://squadair.app/.well-known/security.txt): Machine-readable security vulnerability disclosure contact (`security@squadair.app`).

## Common Questions

- **How does SquadAir compare to Discord or TeamSpeak 6?** Discord relies on Electron/Chromium (`~680+ MB` RAM, `6–12%` CPU overhead in `1080p60` voice+stream scenarios, and restricts 1080p60 screen sharing to paid tiers); TeamSpeak 6 (`~190 MB` RAM) is proprietary. SquadAir is native Rust (`~48 MB` RAM active, `~3.5–6 MB` in tray), free and open source under `GNU AGPLv3`, requires zero accounts, and includes free P2P `1080p60` screen sharing.
- **Do you need an account or central server?** No. Identity keys (`X25519`) and room keys (`ChaCha20-Poly1305` via `BLAKE3`) are generated locally. You can use the public stateless coordinator (`rv.squadair.app:3478`), connect on LAN without internet, or self-host the `1.7 MB` coordinator binary on a single UDP port (`3478`).
